The solar peaks at around 69 kW on a clear day which satisfies the energy usage during regular working hours from March to October. This solar energy is then shifted to keeping the battery charged first and then for export when the battery is fully charged. Future use of the solar is to be fully utilized internally at USU microgrid with little to no export energy due to a large BESS. The USU microgrid system accepts OpenADR signals for the solar when curtailment is needed. Solar curtailment contains safeguards to allow the solar production to return to normal levels after the expiration of the curtailment commands. 6.1.9 Task 9: Enhance Efficiency, Recruitment, and Retention in Participating Buildings 6.1.9.1 Subtask 9.1.0: Implement Efficiency Improvements Six facilities are being evaluated for energy savings based on the new construction building design and additional energy efficiency improvements that were implemented above and beyond code or standard practice. The six facilities include: 7. Soliel Lofts 8. Citizen’s West 9. Project Open II 10. USU EVR and Microgrid 11. Utah Transit Authority Bus Maintenance Building 12. Packsize Existing performance-based programs, such as PacifiCorp’s (Rocky Mountain Power) Wattsmart Energy Efficiency program, continue to drive adoption of efficiency measures. Across the six study buildings, these incentives supported upgrades that achieved more than 30 percent energy savings compared to baseline. These savings were calculated by augmenting BP 1 site studies. At these levels, owner participation has been strong. In parallel, Giv Group has applied lessons from the Project Open buildings to Citizen’s West, and the team was slated to 29 document additional insights from this project to inform future developments that improve both affordability and performance in future budget periods. Additionally, lessons learned from the UDERMS project have resulted in design changes in the development of Citizens West 4. Giv Group, the developer behind Citizen’s West and Open Project buildings, has adjusted equipment selected and building design based on the project learnings. The team had planned to continue to collaborate with Giv Group to review insights gained from UDERMS buildings and document them for future developments. The primary goal of this ongoing effort is to make the apartments even more affordable 6.1.9.2 Subtask 9.2.0 Incentives to encourage efficiency measures and retain occupant participation The project team believed the incentives for energy efficiency measures, as outlined in the PacifiCorp (Rocky Mountain Power) Demand Side Management Program, were sufficient to attract building owners in the future to consider EE measures. However, the team was going to explore additional incentives to encourage customer participation in demand flexibility events, such as using connected thermostats and water heaters. This initiative will enable PacifiCorp to expand its grid service offerings beyond what they currently offer.
